author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: vld_a_q has no reset, so it keeps sampling req_i while rst_a_n holds pay_a_q at zero. The consumer can commit the cleared payload as a valid transfer.

author_reading.rationale: The source valid register has no reset, so it can stay high across rst_a_n while pay_a_q is cleared. The consumer then captures a cleared payload as a real transfer.

labels.rationale: vld_a_q is a valid flop with no reset. It keeps sampling req_i through reset and can release as 1 into the destination reset domain, so held_o can capture stale payload after reset. The same design with vld_a_q reset (c05) is correct.
While the producer is in reset, req_i can still set vld_a_q while pay_a_q is forced to zero. The consumer can commit that reset value as valid.
labels.suspected_flaw: The payload also crosses separate per-bit synchronisers, which cannot assure coherence.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and class, and A's sites are kept. RDC-010 targets the unreset valid feeding a reset register. RDC-005 (both) fires on the reset payload crossing, which the reset-valid twin rfc1-c05 shares, so it does not target this defect.
